newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index premiums erode grudgingly.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index premiums erode grudgingly.

text.p: July premiums on major U.S. stock indexes declined grudgingly Tuesday even though the options expire at the end of the week.

"Even the out-of-the money calls are carrying big premiums going into the expiration," said Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, referring to the S&P 500 .SPX July 925 calls, which traded a heavy 7,320 contracts by about 1230 CDT/1730 GMT.
The July 925 calls were trading down 1/4 at four.
The July 920 calls, with volume of more than 3,900 contracts, slipped 7/8 to six.
"Both are carrying premiums," Schwartz said, citing the July 920 and 925 calls. "They're down but carrying premium."
The spot SPX was up 1.25 at 919.63.

Premiums in out-of-the-money options often decline sharply into expiration as investors give up hope that they will become in-the-money by expiration, but traders said the market's choppiness helped keep premiums firm in the July series despite their short lifespan.
On the put side, the SPX July 920 was most active, with turnover of about 8,090. It fell 1/8 to 6-5/8.
The situation was similar in the S&P 100 .OEX, which was down 0.80 at 895.73.
The most active OEX call was the July 900, with turnover of more than 5,800 contracts. It was down 1-1/4 at five. The July 895 call, which traded about 4,460 contracts, lost 1-1/4 to 7-3/4.
Among OEX puts, the most active was the July 890, which traded about 6,430 contracts. It rose 1/8 to 4-1/4.
The July 895 put traded about 3,605 contracts and gained 3/8 to 6-3/8.
The July 900 put traded about 4,210 contracts. It was up 1-1/4 at 9-1/4.
